problem: A material outcome could disappear when an external GitHub/runtime mutation was rejected before the side effect; blog publication could remain content-ready without terminal repository/deploy/readback closure.
root_cause: The durable obligation was not guaranteed to exist before every external mutation attempt. Execution-surface rejection was treated too close to a terminal blocker instead of a resumable execution interruption. Blog execution identity was not explicitly tied from approved artifact to protected GitHub publisher and production readback.
fix: Require canonical pre-write obligation/checkpoint before every material external mutation.
Classify blocked pre-side-effect writes as RECOVERY_REQUIRED and resume the same idempotency lineage.
Bind daily blog closure to approved artifact -> protected GitHub publisher -> protected merge -> Netlify current-main -> public canonical readback.
Keep LinkedIn company fail-closed only for genuine pre-create write-authority/OAuth denial; organization read/ACL is corroborative and durable provider URN is terminal side-effect evidence.
prevention: No material outcome may rely on a post-failure write to create its own recovery record.
No replacement lineage after a blocked execution-surface write.
No blog LIVE claim without public canonical readback.
No LinkedIn company republish after durable provider URN.
decision: Make the recovery obligation durable before any external mutation and force blocked pre-side-effect writes to resume the same lineage until terminal readback or a genuine hard boundary.
